clue.text: Liberty, a little fraternity and even less equality on the way up

parts.note: a little of the word fraternity: its opening two letters
even less of the word equality than the two letters taken from fraternity: just its opening letter

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the piece is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: A riff on the French revolutionary motto, Liberty, Fraternity, Equality, with the last two shrinking to almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MODE into EDOM, with 'on' a link. The surface borrows the French motto liberte, fraternite, egalite, so Liberty looks like part of the slogan, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberty and freedom are straightforward synonyms for the state of being unconstrained.

clue.text: Lifelines for high-class doctor, here in France about '51

parts.note: U is the old British label for upper-class usage
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: about means the French word goes around the number

parts.note: ici is French for here
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A posh doctor, here in France, around 1951.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the Roman 51 inside the French word for here. The apostrophe in '51 makes it look like a year, 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbilical cords are an unborn baby's literal lifelines, and umbilici is the plural of umbilicus, the navel.

clue.text: Bill needs company doctor to back up agreement

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

indicators.note: in a down clue, to back up means the word is reversed so it reads upwards

explanation.surface: An invoice requires the firm's medic to support a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back up' turns DR into RD.
explanation.definitionFit: An accord is a formal agreement, as between nations or parties to a dispute.

clue.text: Possibly Graham's model is the most environmentally friendly

parts.note: Graham is one possible first name for the novelist Greene, so Graham's could be Greene's
the Model T was Henry Ford's famous car, so T can stand for model

explanation.surface: Perhaps a man called Graham owns the most eco-friendly model.
explanation.walkthrough: Graham Greene was the English novelist; 'Possibly' admits that not every Graham is a Greene.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means environmentally friendly, so its superlative means the most environmentally friendly.

clue.text: Fabrics for kids' coats

parts.note: reads like children's outerwear, but kids are young goats and their skins give a soft napped leather

explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather with a napped finish, traditionally made from kid skin, so it is literally a kid's coat.

clue.text: The going rate for operational centre?

indicators.note: going here means changing, so the letters of rate are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks what the current price might be for a working hub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' rearranges RATE into ATRE. 'The going rate' reads as a stock phrase for a price, hiding the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating theatre is the room where surgeons operate, so it is the centre of operations in a hospital.

clue.text: I'm taking cricketing doctor outside, with a wry face

indicators.note: outside means the doctor's name goes around the other piece

parts.note: W G Grace was the famous Victorian cricketer who was also a medical doctor
I'm gives its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a cricket-playing medic while pulling a sour expression.
explanation.walkthrough: W G Grace was England's most famous nineteenth-century cricketer and a qualified doctor. 'taking' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression, which is what a wry face is.

clue.text: A drink for the doctor! Anything at all!

parts.note: DR is the standard abbreviation for doctor
aught is an old word meaning anything whatever

explanation.surface: A medic orders a drink and will take whatever is going.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a single swallow or a measure of drink, as in a sleeping draught.

clue.text: Because of these fellows' activities, a drug costs a mint

definitions.text: Because of these fellows' activities, a drug costs a mint

indicators.note: to mint is to make or coin something new, so the letters are formed afresh

explanation.surface: Thanks to the patrol men's work at sea, smuggled narcotics fetch a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mint' signals the anagram of A DRUG COSTS A. Read as a whole, the clue also describes the men: by stopping smuggling they make drugs scarce and dear.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastguards patrol the shore to stop smuggling, which pushes up the street price of drugs.

clue.text: Mice do mutate, as shown by the doctor

indicators.note: to mutate is to change form, so the letters of the two words change their order

explanation.surface: A lab note on mice that mutate, as a medic observes.
explanation.definitionFit: Medico is an informal word for a doctor or medical student.

clue.text: Ring minister back — doctor wants a direction to use chequebook excessively

parts.note: O is the shape of a ring

indicators.note: back means the minister's title is written backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a title for a minister of religion
W stands for west, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Phone the vicar again; the doctor needs telling how to spend beyond his means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REV into VER.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdraw an account is to write cheques for more money than it holds.

clue.text: Ian Fleming's doctor died before one, causing complications

parts.note: Dr No is the villain of Ian Fleming's James Bond novel
d is the abbreviation for died in genealogies and obituaries
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The Bond villain dies first, and trouble follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' and 'causing' just link the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodi is the plural of nodus, a knotty point or complication in a plot or argument.

clue.text: Is writer's journal missing one about doctor's source of medication?

indicators.note: about means the shortened journal goes around the other letters
missing means a letter is taken out of the journal

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal
I is the Roman numeral for one
a pen is a writer, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: Asks whether a writer's diary has lost something regarding a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes I out of the journal to leave DARY, and 'about' wraps that round the other letters. 'Doctor's' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispensary is the place where medicines are made up and handed out, often attached to a surgery.

clue.text: Doctor presumed to be cohabiting with Sharon in Hollywood

parts.note: living together means cohabiting, so living can stand for it
Sharon Stone is a Hollywood film actress

explanation.surface: Gossip that a doctor is shacked up with a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley's 'Dr Livingstone, I presume?' on finding the explorer in Africa is the famous line behind 'Doctor presumed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish missionary-explorer is the doctor famously greeted with 'I presume' by Henry Morton Stanley.

clue.text: Puzzle concerning eyes said to need urgent treatment

indicators.note: a treatment is a working-over, so the letters are reworked
said means the word eyes is taken by how it is spoken, as two letter I's

parts.note: eyes, said out loud, are I's

explanation.surface: A question about eyes that apparently need immediate care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns eyes into II, and 'treatment' scrambles II with URGENT. 'concerning' and 'to need' are links; 'urgent treatment' looks like a medical phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrigue is to puzzle or arouse curiosity in someone; as a verb the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: Newborn is a long time in the province

indicators.note: in means the long period sits inside the province's name

parts.note: Natal was a province of South Africa
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: A baby is an age away in a distant province.
explanation.walkthrough: Natal, now KwaZulu-Natal, was a province of South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Neonatal describes the first weeks after birth, so it means relating to the newborn.

clue.text: Enlarge building for public use

indicators.note: building means making something, so the letters are constructed anew

explanation.surface: A plan to extend a public building.
explanation.definitionFit: General can mean open to all or common, as in a general hospital or general admission.

clue.text: Something a car might need — agent isn't in ignorance

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
ain't is the uneducated form of isn't

explanation.surface: A car salesman who hasn't a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh coat of paint is a typical need for a scratched or faded car.

clue.text: Some doctors relax (in private) right before a sister returns

indicators.note: in means the soldier goes inside the word for relax

parts.note: to rest is to relax
a GI is an American private soldier

indicators.note: returns means the abbreviation is turned back to front

parts.note: Sr is the abbreviation for Sister, as in a nun's title

explanation.surface: Medics unwind behind closed doors before a nurse comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns SR into RS. 'Private' looks like an adjective in the surface, but it is the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A registrar is a hospital doctor in specialist training, ranking below a consultant.

clue.text: The laziest I'd put first — in case …

indicators.note: put first places the opening piece ahead of the next one

parts.note: I'd gives its letters without the apostrophe
lest means in case, as in lest we forget

explanation.surface: Someone apologising that they put the idlest first, just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots carry the sentence into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means lazy, so idlest is the laziest, a straight superlative synonym.

clue.text: … it could be messy — getting square with the powers that be

indicators.note: it could be signals that the letters might be arranged into another word

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing tool, so T can stand for square

explanation.surface: Continuing from the clue before, things may get untidy when you square up to authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it could be' scrambles MESSY with T. 'getting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The system, as in fighting the system, is the established authority, the powers that be.

clue.text: Warning for doctor going back to topless bird

indicators.note: going back means the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: MO, Medical Officer, is a military doctor

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a hen is a bird

explanation.surface: A caution for a doctor returning to a lady with no top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns MO into OM; 'topless' takes H off HEN, leaving EN.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign or warning of what is to come.

clue.text: Flier to ring doctor back about vitamin

parts.note: to ring is to sound a bell
B1 is a vitamin, thiamine, written here with I for the figure 1

indicators.note: back means the doctor's abbreviation is reversed

explanation.surface: Phone the doctor back about a vitamin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the doctor. 'about' only loosely places the reversed doctor next to the vitamin; it is a link word here, not a container. The bellbird is not a British bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The bellbird is a bird of Australia, New Zealand or South America named for its bell-like call, so a flier.

clue.text: Witch doctor has transformed the fellow

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters of has are rearranged

parts.note: a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A medicine man has changed his patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges HAS into SHA.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal healer and spirit medium, which is what a witch doctor is.

clue.text: Which doctor makes endless ado about short Australian

indicators.note: about means the cut-down fuss goes around the other piece
endless means the last letter of the word is taken off

parts.note: fuss and ado both mean commotion

indicators.note: short means the word is cut down to its common abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written before it is shortened

explanation.surface: Asks which medic is making a fuss about an Aussie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the fuss to FUS, and 'short' trims Australian to AUST before 'about' wraps one round the other. 'Which doctor' plays on witch doctor from the clue before.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Faustus is Marlowe's play about the scholar who sells his soul to the devil.

clue.text: Holds up doctor instead

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are changed round

explanation.surface: A medic stands in for someone delayed.
explanation.definitionFit: To detain someone is to hold them up or delay them.
